subject: SIG: Deployment provenance & secrets governance — follow-up
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finservco.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: sig-portal@assessor.io
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: provenance for recent deploys and secrets handling

Hi Markus —

Thanks again for the quick walkthrough last week. As a follow-up for the SIG assessment team, can you provide a compact provenance package that shows: 

- the change-approval trail for the three deploys we flagged (2029-06-10, 2029-06-28, 2029-07-18),
- CI artifact origins (which builder job + commit + container digest), and
- proof that ephemeral tokens used by the CI jobs are sampled and rotated per your control matrix?

We mostly need machine-readable exports where possible (csv/json) and a short executive summary that calls out any manual signoffs. If there are any known gaps, flag them so we can document compensating controls.

Appreciate it — target for delivery is COB tomorrow (2029-07-30) if feasible.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Senior Assessor — FinServ Compliance
alice.chen@finservco.com

--
Attachment requests: export of your CI run metadata, ephemeral-token sampling report, and change log export (machine readable preferred).

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finservco.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sig-portal@assessor.io
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: provenance for recent deploys and secrets handling

Hi Alice —

Thanks — we can assemble this. High-level status: we have the CI artifact chronology export and token-sampling summary ready for ingestion; the change-approval audit is a filtered export and will need a short readme to explain fields. I'll attach the exports and a brief narrative.

Quick notes up front so the team knows what to expect:
- Artifact chronology maps builder job -> git commit SHA -> image digest and timestamp. We include the signing step metadata when present.
- Ephemeral token sampling: we rotate CI ephemeral creds via our vault integrator every 6 hours and log issuance events. The summary shows sampling frequency and redaction for tokens.
- Change approvals: we export PR approvals + canary rollout timestamps. Manual signoffs are flagged where required (security approvals for feature flags).

I'll send the artifact files in a follow-up (zipped) email and paste the key CSV/summary below. If you need native access, I'll put a copy in the Drive link (will share).

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: readme-evidence-index.txt]

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finservco.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Delivering exports: CI artifact chronology + token sampling summary + change log export

Alice — attaching the requested exports. See short summary below and a pointer to the Drive bundle.

Attachments included (machine-readable):
- redwood-ci-artifact-chronology.csv — columns: deploy_date, builder_job, commit_sha, image_digest, signed (true/false), signature_meta_id
- ephemeral-token-sampling-summary.pdf — executive summary + sampling table (redacted token ids)
- change-approval-log-export.jsonl — newline-delimited JSON of approval events (timestamp, actor, pr_id, approval_type)
- readme-evidence-index.txt — mapping of file fields and filters used

Executive summary (short):
- For the three flagged deploys, builder_job IDs map to commits and digests without gaps. We observed a single manual security approval on 2029-06-28 for a feature-flag change (actor: s.security).
- Ephemeral tokens: issuance events sampled show rotation on average every 5.8 hours for active runners; sampling window is configurable and was set to 6 hours for the audit period. No anomalies in issuance counts.
- Change approvals export includes both automated approvals (CI bots) and human approvals; manual signoffs are labeled with approval_type=human.

Drive bundle: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/sig/FIN-2029-0472/evidence (shared read-only link)

If you want a flattened csv of the change-approval export, Jordan and Marissa can generate it with the filters you want.

Regards,
Markus

[attachment: ephemeral-token-sampling-summary.pdf]

From: Mark Reynolds <mark.reynolds@assessor.io>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@finservco.com>, sig-portal@assessor.io
Date: Mon, 29 Jul 2029 17:25:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Delivering exports: CI artifact chronology + token sampling summary + change log export

Markus / team —

Received the bundle, thank you. A couple of small clarifications so we can ingest cleanly into the SIG portal: 

1) In change-approval-log-export.jsonl we see approval_type values: human|bot|auto. Can you confirm the canonical mapping for 'auto' vs 'bot'? We want to ensure 'auto' means an automated process (e.g., scheduled merge) and 'bot' indicates a machine actor that can vote (e.g., dependabot).

2) For the ephemeral-token-sampling-summary.pdf, can you provide the underlying CSV used to create the sampling table (redacted token id, issuance_ts, issuer_actor, rotation_interval_minutes)? The PDF is clear but the portal prefers structured CSV for traceability.

3) One more ask: can you include the Git signing metadata for the two commits that show signed=true in the artifact chronology? A small field: gpg_key_fingerprint or sig_meta_id that maps to signature store.

If you can drop those as separate CSVs/exports into the Drive folder we can finish ingestion today.

Thanks,
Mark Reynolds
Principal Assessor — SIG Team
assessor.io

Hi Mark / Alice —

Thanks for the quick review. Action items completed and uploaded to the same Drive bundle:

- change-approval-human-vs-bot-mapping.csv — canonical mapping (auto=system scheduled actions; bot=named CI bots that vote)
- token-sampling-raw.csv — columns: redacted_token_id, issuance_ts, issuer_actor, rotation_interval_minutes (redaction applied to token_id column)
- git-signature-mapping.csv — columns: commit_sha, gpg_key_fingerprint, sig_meta_id (links to signature store entries)

Notes: the token-sampling CSV has a sampling window of 2029-06-01..2029-07-31 per your requested scope. The git-signature-mapping has entries for the two signed commits referenced in the chronology.

Drive link (same): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/sig/FIN-2029-0472/evidence — I also set folder permissions for your assessor accounts (read-only).

If anything else is needed for ingestion into the portal, flag it and Jordan will produce a flattened CSV of the approval export.

Regards,
